kept.heading: WHAT'S WORKING IN B2B GTM IN 2026 (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Founder-led sales remains a leading GTM motion until companies reach $10M ARR. Networking and introductions rank as the most effective channel, while intimate events come second. AI search is now a core channel for 39% of B2B companies, up 11 percentage points year over year, and 41% are experimenting with it. Track whether AI tools recommend the right products and pricing. Use buying signals such as content engagement and website visits to prioritize outreach.

kept.heading: CITIZENLAB DETAILS NEW SPYWARE TRIGGERED BY ONLINE ADVERTISING (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Discover-Tech, an Israeli firm presenting itself as an ad vendor, displayed 442 million ads on more than 120,000 websites and apps, including the BBC, The New York Times, and Duolingo. Some of those ads carried zero-click spyware that infected phones and computers simply by appearing on screen, with targets ranging from Al Jazeera journalists to NATO and NVIDIA staff. It is the first confirmed case of government-backed zero-click spyware delivered through online ads. Google has since blocked Discover-Tech from its ad platforms.

kept.heading: HOW TO PITCH LOCAL NEWSROOMS IN THE US (9 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Local news pitches are more effective when they target the right journalist, demonstrate a clear community impact, and provide everything needed to produce the story. Local newsrooms have declined by 81% since 2002, making relevant, ready-to-use pitches especially important. Start by reviewing journalists' recent coverage, then contact assignment editors at TV stations or editors at print and digital outlets when appropriate. Tailor pitches to the format: print needs a clear story and supporting data, TV needs visuals and local people to interview, and radio needs an available guest who can speak. Include a timely local angle, relevant data, quotes, visuals, and event details, and send the pitch before the newsroom's morning planning meeting.

kept.heading: WHY BRANDS NEED TO FUEL A LIFE, NOT FILL A FEED (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Pinterest reports that 40% of Gen Z wish social media had never been invented and 63% intentionally unplug. Design campaigns that drive real-world action rather than endless scrolling. Show how a product fits into the audience's desired lifestyle instead of making the product the hero. Turn inspiration into action with personalized recommendations and specific next steps such as shopping lists or linked outfits. Remove friction with tools that help people follow through.

kept.heading: THE ART OF BRAND MERCH (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: People wear merch to say something about themselves, not to promote a company. A logo on a T-shirt or water bottle asks customers to carry a message without giving them a reason, and only works when the logo already means something. Strong merch does one of three jobs. It signals belonging through a recognizable color or shape, sells more product by being designed around how that product gets used, or lets in people who can't yet afford the core product.

kept.heading: HOW LONG SHOULD A REEL BE? UNDER 3 MINUTES ON INSTAGRAM, LONGER ON TIKTOK (12 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Video length barely matters on Instagram until the 3-minute mark, where recommendations to new audiences stop. Reels from 10 seconds to 3 minutes all perform within 2% of each creator's median, while longer ones fall to 0.91x. TikTok rewards length instead, with 3-to-10-minute videos earning 1.22x and beating the same creator's 10-to-19-second clips for 68% of creators.

kept.heading: YOUR NEWSLETTER ISN'T THE UNSUBSCRIBE PROBLEM (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google Postmaster Tools evaluates unsubscribe compliance across all email systems sending from the same domain. If someone unsubscribes from a newsletter but still receives CRM or sales emails, Google may flag the domain. Sync unsubscribe lists across platforms and use distinct From addresses and List-IDs for each mailing list. Verify that every system supports one-click unsubscribes and removes recipients within 48 hours. Compliance status can take 1-2 weeks to update.

kept.heading: A STANDING HOLDOUT IS THE ONLY AUDIT AN ALGORITHM CANNOT ARGUE WITH (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Standing holdouts are a measurement method that reserves a portion of markets or audiences from automated ad campaigns to measure whether advertising generates incremental sales. Uber cut $100 million of its $150 million annual rider acquisition budget without reducing app installs, while Airbnb recovered to 95% of its 2019 traffic levels before resuming marketing spend. A standing holdout reserves 5% to 10% of markets and rotates them on a fixed schedule to measure advertising performance over time. Each test defines its markets, measurement period, success thresholds, and budget decisions in advance. If holdout results conflict with the platform's reported returns beyond a predefined margin, the holdout results determine budget decisions.

kept.heading: AI AGENTS BUY THROUGH YOUR OWN CHECKOUT, AND DISPUTES STILL LAND ON YOU (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: In-chat AI checkouts are built for physical goods sold to US buyers through big platforms. Google, Microsoft, and ChatGPT all exclude subscriptions or say nothing about them. Independent sellers instead meet agents like Amazon's Buy for Me and Meta's Muse on their own checkout pages, where guest purchase and saved-wallet support decide whether an order completes. Visa bars merchants from requiring dispute waivers on agent purchases, so chargebacks still land on the seller.

kept.heading: YOUR TEAM SAYS AI SAVES THEM TIME. HERE'S HOW TO FIND OUT IF IT DOES (15 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The best way to measure AI value is to measure it against a control group.

kept.heading: AMAZON LAUNCHES NEW BEE ‘PERSONAL AI' DEVICES THAT LISTEN TO CONVERSATIONS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Unlike Echo, which waits for a wake word, the new devices record continuously to build conversation summaries and recurring-theme goals.

kept.heading: TELLING AI TO ACT AS YOUR CUSTOMERS MAKES ITS ANSWER WORSE (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI-generated customer personas can overestimate purchase intent and mislead product or campaign decisions. In one test, AI predicted that 52% of shoppers would buy a product when only 33% did. In another, AI personas were less accurate at predicting headline clicks than a model asked directly to choose which headlines readers would click.

kept.heading: GOOGLE'S WHEN TO BUY GUIDE (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google's 2026 holiday shopping guide uses historical pricing data to identify when discounts peak across retail categories. Black Friday weekend offers the best selection and savings for electronics, shoes, fragrances, and appliances. Late December brings deeper discounts on cosmetics, handbags, and kitchenware. Search data also reveals last-minute shopping patterns. “Next day shipping” searches peak December 22, while “same day pickup” peaks December 24.

kept.heading: GATED CONTENT IS THE #1 ENEMY OF AI SEARCH (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Ungate content that helps buyers research categories and compare vendors to improve AI search visibility. Reserve forms for genuinely exclusive assets such as personalized ROI audits and proprietary data. For research reports, publish key findings and methodology on an accessible landing page while gating the full download. Noindex gated landing pages and hosted PDFs when appropriate to prevent them from competing with primary website content.

kept.heading: YOUR NEXT MARKETING HIRE SHOULD PROBABLY SURPRISE YOU (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: As AI makes content production cheaper and product comparisons easier, brands need to stand out during the awareness stage. Viral Producers test entertaining campaigns that get people talking about a brand. Internet Comedians create culturally relevant content people want to share. Creator Deal Makers build partnerships that help creators grow their audiences while expanding brand reach. These roles help brands earn attention rather than compete on content volume alone.

kept.heading: HOW TO AUTOMATE CONTENT CREATION: A FOLLOW-ALONG GUIDE (16 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Ahrefs built an AI workflow that updates 12 data-driven articles monthly by refreshing search data and rebuilding tables and charts in WordPress drafts. Its guide shows how to automate repetitive content tasks by documenting workflows and connecting reliable data sources. It recommends testing one workflow at a time and keeping human review before publication to catch errors and prevent broken automations from publishing inaccurate content.

kept.heading: HOW THE AI BOOM MIGHT REALLY END: 5 SCENARIOS (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The AI boom may end not because demand disappears, but because profits shift away from major AI labs. Open-weight models are driving prices down while efficiency breakthroughs could reduce computing costs. AI companies risk failing to capture the value they create while chipmakers and infrastructure providers could still benefit from growing AI usage even if leading AI labs lose value.

kept.heading: WHAT ON EARTH IS GOING ON WITH AI PRICING AND PACKAGING? (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI companies are struggling to price products because usage costs vary widely and customers can't predict what credits or tokens will buy them. ChatGPT and Claude advertise vague usage limits, while Lovable sells credits without explaining what customers can build with them. Unlike traditional SaaS pricing based on seats or transactions, AI costs depend on the complexity of each task and the resources needed to complete it. Companies must make usage limits and costs easier to understand while managing unpredictable computing expenses and preventing abuse of free plans.

kept.heading: CHATGPT ADVERTISERS REPORT MIXED RESULTS AS TARGETING PROBLEMS PERSIST (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 14% of ChatGPT ads have limited or no connection to the user's query.

kept.heading: BOTS USED TO BE A THREAT. NOW THEY'RE YOUR CUSTOMERS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands today need to optimize websites for AI shopping agents to improve product discovery.
